mainTopic: The נשיא and אב בית דין of the זוגות, מנחם's departure, and the laws of סמיכה on יום טוב
overview: The amud opens with the end of the משנה: in each of the five זוגות, the first-named sage was the נשיא and the second was the אב בית דין. A ברייתא brings רבי מאיר's way of deciding who was נשיא, and the חכמים say that שמעון בן שטח, not יהודה בן טבאי, was the נשיא. The גמרא then tells the story of יהודה בן טבאי executing a single עד זומם, being rebuked by שמעון בן שטח, and promising to rule only in his presence. The גמרא tries to use that promise to show the story follows רבי מאיר, but answers that it fits the חכמים too. Next, the גמרא explains that מנחם left the בית דין, either to go astray (אביי) or to serve the king (רבא), and a ברייתא supports רבא. רבי יוחנן teaches never to take a שבות lightly, since the great sages argued about סמיכה on יום טוב. רמי בר חמא learns that סמיכה needs all one's strength, and the גמרא defends this against a ברייתא about women doing סמיכה. Finally, רב פפא learns from that story that using the sides of an animal is also forbidden.

steps.title: The משנה: first of each pair was נשיא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by saying the first-named sage in each pair was the נשיא and the second was the אב בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first ones were נשיאים, and the ones second to them were heads of the court.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the משנה. It tells us the job of each sage in the five זוגות it listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed five pairs of leaders who argued about סמיכה. Now it adds who held which post: the first-named in each pair was the נשיא, and the second was the אב בית דין, the deputy.

keyTerms.meaning: The head of the סנהדרין
Head of the court; the deputy to the נשיא
The five pairs of leaders of the generations

phrases.english: The first ones were נשיאים,
phrases.notes: The first-named sage in each of the five pairs the משנה just listed.

phrases.english: and the ones second to them were heads of the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of the זוגות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In each pair, the first-named was נשיא and the second was אב בית דין.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the נשיא is decided by his position on סמיכה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי מאיר: in the first three pairs, the one who said not to do סמיכה was נשיא. In the last two pairs, the one who said to do סמיכה was נשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: In the first three pairs, those who said not to lean hands, and in the last two pairs, those who said to lean hands, were the נשיאים. The others were heads of court. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with רבי מאיר's way of identifying which sage in each pair was the נשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר does not go simply by who is named first. He links the post to each sage's opinion on סמיכה on יום טוב. In the early pairs, the sage who forbade it was נשיא. In the later pairs, the sage who required it was נשיא.

keyTerms.meaning: To lean one's hands on a קרבן (סמיכה)

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
three of the first pairs,
the ones who said not to lean hands,
and two of the last pairs,
the ones who said to lean hands —
(the first ones) were נשיאים,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: and the ones second to them were heads of the court,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that explains the משנה's statement about who was נשיא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the first three pairs, the sage who forbade סמיכה was נשיא. In the last two pairs, the sage who permitted it was נשיא.

steps.title: The חכמים: שמעון בן שטח was the נשיא
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree about the third pair. They say יהודה בן טבאי was אב בית דין and שמעון בן שטח was נשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages say: יהודה בן טבאי was head of the court, and שמעון בן שטח was נשיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give the opposite view about the third pair, the pair of יהודה בן טבאי and שמעון בן שטח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, יהודה בן טבאי forbade סמיכה and was in one of the first three pairs, so he was נשיא. The חכמים reverse this: שמעון בן שטח was the נשיא, and יהודה בן טבאי was his deputy.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Sages say; this introduces the opposing view
One of the third pair of leaders
His partner in the third pair

steps.whatToRemember: There is a מחלוקת: רבי מאיר holds that יהודה בן טבאי was נשיא, and the חכמים hold that שמעון בן שטח was נשיא.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: יְהוּדָה בֶּן טָבַאי — אַב בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.english: יהודה בן טבאי was head of the court,
and שמעון בן שטח was נשיא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: יְהוּדָה בֶּן טָבַאי אַב בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר about the third pair
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמעון בן שטח was נשיא and יהודה בן טבאי was אב בית דין.

steps.title: Which תנא taught the following ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which side of the dispute, רבי מאיר or the חכמים, is behind the ברייתא it is about to quote.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who taught this, which the Rabbis taught:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to quote a story and wants to know which view of who was נשיא that story fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story that follows shows how יהודה בן טבאי and שמעון בן שטח related to each other. The גמרא wants to use it to see which opinion it follows. Steps 10–12 take up this question after the full story, and in the end the story fits both views.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא? A question asking whose view a source follows

phrases.english: Who is the תנא who taught this, which the Rabbis taught:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which side of the מחלוקת a different ברייתא follows
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the coming ברייתא follows רבי מאיר or the חכמים on who was נשיא.

steps.title: יהודה בן טבאי executes a false witness to oppose the צדוקים
steps.stepSummary: יהודה בן טבאי swears that he executed an עד זומם. He did it to oppose the צדוקים, who said עדים זוממין are only killed if the accused was already killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן טבאי said: May I not see the consolation if I did not kill a false witness. I did it to remove the view of the צדוקים from their hearts, for they would say: False witnesses are not killed until the accused has been killed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא begins its story. יהודה בן טבאי proudly reports that he executed an עד זומם to prove the צדוקים wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צדוקים held that false witnesses are only executed after their victim was actually executed. Our tradition holds the opposite: they are executed only if the victim was not yet executed. To make this point publicly, יהודה בן טבאי executed a false witness before the accused was killed.

keyTerms.meaning: May I see consolation; a form of oath
A false witness proven false by other witnesses who say he was elsewhere
The צדוקים, a sect that rejected the Oral Torah
The accused person who was judged

steps.confusionAlert: The צדוקים' rule is the reverse of the הלכה. In our הלכה, עדים זוממין are killed only if the accused was NOT yet killed.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה בן טבאי said:
May I see the consolation,
phrases.notes: This is an oath: may I not see the consolation of Israel if what I say is untrue.

phrases.english: if I did not kill a false witness,
to remove it from the hearts of the צדוקים.
For they would say:
false witnesses are not killed
until the accused has been killed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן טָבַאי: אֶרְאֶה בְּנֶחָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the ברייתא the question asked about
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהודה בן טבאי executed an עד זומם before the accused was killed, to oppose the צדוקים.

steps.title: שמעון בן שטח: you killed an innocent man
steps.stepSummary: שמעון בן שטח tells יהודה בן טבאי that he shed innocent blood. Both witnesses must be proven false before either one is punished.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמעון בן שטח said to him: May I not see the consolation if you did not shed innocent blood. The Sages said: False witnesses are not killed until both are proven false, they are not flogged until both are proven false, and they do not pay money until both are proven false.
steps.whatsHappening: שמעון בן שטח strongly objects to what יהודה בן טבאי did, and swears that he killed an innocent man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהודה בן טבאי executed only one witness, after only that one was proven false. The הלכה is that the pair of witnesses works as one unit. If only one is proven false, no punishment applies to him, whether death, lashes, or money.

keyTerms.meaning: Innocent blood
That both of them are proven to be זוממין
They receive lashes

steps.whatToRemember: עדים זוממין receive no punishment of any kind, whether death, lashes, or money, unless both witnesses are proven false.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rebuke leads to יהודה בן טבאי's promise in step 7. The גמרא uses that promise in steps 10–12 to test whether the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר or the חכמים.

phrases.english: שמעון בן שטח said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֶרְאֶה בְּנֶחָמָה אִם לֹא שָׁפַכְתָּ דָּם נָקִי,
phrases.english: May I see the consolation if you did not shed innocent blood,
for the Sages said:
false witnesses are not killed
until both of them are proven false,
and they are not flogged until both of them are proven false,
and they do not pay money
until both of them are proven false.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטַח: אֶרְאֶה בְּנֶחָמָה אִם לֹא שָׁפַכְתָּ דָּם נָקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמעון בן שטח attacks the execution described in the previous step
steps.kashyaTarget: יהודה בן טבאי's execution of a single עד זומם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Punishment of עדים זוממין requires that both witnesses be proven false. Executing one witness alone means killing someone who was not legally guilty.

steps.title: יהודה בן טבאי accepts that he will rule only before שמעון בן שטח
steps.stepSummary: After he is rebuked, יהודה בן טבאי takes on himself never to rule on הלכה unless שמעון בן שטח is present.
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away, יהודה בן טבאי accepted on himself that he would not rule on הלכה except in front of שמעון בן שטח.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on with the story. יהודה בן טבאי reacts to שמעון בן שטח's sharp rebuke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He sees he made a terrible mistake, so he promises to rule only with שמעון בן שטח watching. This detail will matter later. The גמרא will use it to work out who held which position.

keyTerms.meaning: He accepted on himself, he took on a commitment
Rules on a question of Jewish law
In the presence of

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא uses this promise in steps 10 and 11 to try to show that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר. Step 12 answers that the promise fits the חכמים too.

phrases.aramaic: מִיָּד קִבֵּל עָלָיו יְהוּדָה בֶּן טָבַאי
phrases.english: Immediately Yehuda ben Tabbai accepted upon himself
that he would not rule on halacha
except in the presence of Shimon ben Shatach.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד קִבֵּל עָלָיו יְהוּדָה בֶּן טָבַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how יהודה בן טבאי responded to the rebuke in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהודה בן טבאי promised to rule only in the presence of שמעון בן שטח.

steps.title: יהודה בן טבאי weeps at the grave of the executed man
steps.stepSummary: For the rest of his life, יהודה בן טבאי lay on the executed man's grave, and his crying could be heard. He told the people it was his own voice, and that it would stop once he died.
steps.simpleTranslation: All his life, יהודה בן טבאי would lie on the grave of the man he executed, and his voice could be heard. People thought it was the dead man's voice. He told them: It is my voice. You will know this, because once he dies his voice will not be heard anymore.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more part of the story. It shows how sorry יהודה בן טבאי was for the rest of his life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People thought the dead man was crying out from his grave. יהודה בן טבאי says it is really his own crying. He offers a sign: when 'he' dies, the voice will stop. He means himself, but he says it in an indirect way.

keyTerms.meaning: Lay stretched out face-down, prostrated himself
The man who was executed
They thought, they assumed
You will know, here is the proof

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל יָמָיו שֶׁל יְהוּדָה בֶּן טָבַאי
phrases.english: All the days of Yehuda ben Tabbai
he would prostrate himself on the grave
of that executed man,
phrases.notes: This is the עד זומם from step 5, the one שמעון בן שטח said was innocent.

phrases.english: and his voice was heard.
The people thought to say
that it was the voice of the executed man.
He said to them: It is my voice.
Know it, for tomorrow he will die,
phrases.notes: 'He' means יהודה בן טבאי himself. He just didn't want to say 'I will die' out loud.

phrases.english: and his voice will not be heard.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל יָמָיו שֶׁל יְהוּדָה בֶּן טָבַאי הָיָה מִשְׁתַּטֵּחַ עַל קִבְרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes on with the story of how יהודה בן טבאי showed regret.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The voice at the grave was יהודה בן טבאי's, and the proof is that it would stop when he died.

steps.title: רב אחא בר רבא questions the proof from the voice stopping
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא says the voice stopping proves nothing. Maybe the dead man was appeased, or maybe he took his case to the Heavenly court.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רבא, said to רב אשי: But maybe יהודה בן טבאי made peace with him, or maybe the dead man brought him to judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא challenges the 'proof' given in the story. The voice stopping after יהודה בן טבאי's death does not show whose voice it was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story's proof was this: if the voice stops when יהודה בן טבאי dies, it must have been his. רב אחא offers other reasons the dead man's voice could stop at that time. Maybe יהודה בן טבאי made peace with him in the next world. Or maybe the dead man finally got his case judged in Heaven. Either way, there was no more reason for the dead man to cry out.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
He fully appeased him, made peace with him
He sued him in judgment, took him to court

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
But perhaps he appeased him,
phrases.notes: Meaning יהודה בן טבאי made peace with the dead man in the next world after he died.

phrases.english: or he sued him in judgment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered at the end of step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof that the voice belonged to יהודה בן טבאי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The voice could stop for other reasons: the dead man was appeased, or he got justice in the Heavenly court.

steps.title: The story fits רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to its question of whose view the ברייתא follows. It shows that the story fits רבי מאיר, who made יהודה בן טבאי the נשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this ברייתא? It works well if you say רבי מאיר. He said שמעון בן שטח was the אב בית דין and יהודה בן טבאי was the נשיא. That explains why יהודה בן טבאי had been ruling in front of שמעון בן שטח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the question from step 4. It shows that the story fits smoothly with רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי מאיר, יהודה בן טבאי was the נשיא, the higher position. So it made sense for him to rule even when שמעון בן שטח was there. His promise to rule only with שמעון בן שטח present was a real change from how he had acted before.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this?
It works well if you say
Head of the court, second to the נשיא
That is why, that explains

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this?
It is fine if you say Rabbi Meir,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטַח אַב בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.english: who said Shimon ben Shatach was av beit din,
Rabbi Yehuda ben Tabbai was Nasi
that is why he was ruling halacha
in the presence of Shimon ben Shatach.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי הָא? אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא, רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side point in step 9 and goes back to the question from step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יהודה בן טבאי ruled in front of שמעון בן שטח, which makes sense only if he was the נשיא.

steps.title: The story is hard to fit with the חכמים' view
steps.stepSummary: Under the חכמים, יהודה בן טבאי was only the אב בית דין. An אב בית דין would not rule in front of the נשיא anyway, so the story makes no sense under their view.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say the ברייתא follows the חכמים, who said יהודה בן טבאי was the אב בית דין and שמעון בן שטח was the נשיא, there is a problem. Would an אב בית דין ever rule on הלכה in front of the נשיא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges reading the ברייתא as the view of the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שמעון בן שטח was the נשיא, יהודה בן טבאי, as the lower אב בית דין, should not have been ruling in front of him in the first place. So his promise to rule only in front of שמעון בן שטח would not make sense. The question is rhetorical: obviously an אב בית דין does not rule in front of the נשיא.

keyTerms.meaning: But if you say
The חכמים, the Sages
Does he? (opens a question that expects 'no')

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not why he promised to rule in front of שמעון בן שטח. It is that under the חכמים he should never have been ruling in front of him at all.

phrases.english: But if you say the Rabbanan, who say:

phrases.aramaic: יְהוּדָה בֶּן טָבַאי אַב בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.english: Yehuda ben Tabbai was av beit din,
Shimon ben Shatach was Nasi
an av beit din, in the presence of a Nasi,
does he rule halacha?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the 'it works well for one side, but for the other side' comparison started in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the ברייתא as following the חכמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An אב בית דין does not rule in front of the נשיא, so under the חכמים יהודה בן טבאי would never have been ruling in front of שמעון בן שטח. That makes his promise pointless.

steps.title: His vow was about not even joining a vote
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge. Even under the חכמים, יהודה בן טבאי's vow makes sense: he took on not even to join other judges in a ruling until he heard שמעון בן שטח.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. What did he mean by 'he took upon himself'? He meant joining others: 'Even joining others in a ruling, I will not join.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 11. It shows the story can fit the חכמים too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said an אב בית דין would never rule alone in front of the נשיא anyway, so his vow would add nothing. The answer is that his vow went further. He would not even add his vote to other judges until שמעון בן שטח had spoken. So the vow was a real new step, even for an אב בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: He took upon himself (a personal vow or commitment)
To join together (with other judges in a ruling)
I will not join

steps.whatToRemember: The story of יהודה בן טבאי can fit both רבי מאיר and the חכמים. Under the חכמים, his vow was that he would not even join a group ruling without שמעון בן שטח.

phrases.english: No; what is the meaning of 'he took upon himself' that he said?
It is about joining others.
phrases.notes: He means adding his vote to the other judges' ruling, not ruling all by himself.

phrases.english: That even to join as well,
I will not join.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 11 by giving a new meaning to the vow.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His vow meant he would not rule alone, and an אב בית דין would not do that in front of the נשיא anyway.
steps.terutzMaskana: His vow meant he would not even join a group ruling until שמעון בן שטח had spoken.

steps.title: Where did מנחם go?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that מנחם left and שמאי took his place. It asks where מנחם went.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'מנחם left and שמאי entered,' and so on. Where did he go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and asks a question about it. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says that מנחם 'left,' with no details. The גמרא wants to know what that leaving was. That would explain why שמאי replaced him.

keyTerms.meaning: To where?

phrases.english: 'מנחם left and שמאי entered,' and so on.
To where did he leave?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, after the story of יהודה בן טבאי is finished.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What 'מנחם left' means: where he went and why.

steps.title: אביי: he went astray
steps.stepSummary: אביי says מנחם left and went down a bad path.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: He left and went astray.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the first answer: מנחם left the Torah path.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under אביי, 'left' means a spiritual fall, not a change of job. This would explain why the משנה gives no details about it.

keyTerms.meaning: A bad way of life; going astray

phrases.english: אביי said:
He left for a bad way of life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question of Step 13.

steps.title: רבא: he went into the king's service
steps.stepSummary: רבא says מנחם left to work for the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: He left for the king's service.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second, different answer: מנחם took a job working for the king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבא, מנחם did not fall spiritually. He took a government post, so he could no longer sit in the בית דין, and שמאי replaced him.

keyTerms.meaning: The king's service; a royal government post

phrases.english: רבא said:
He left for the king's service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from אביי's to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מנחם went to serve the king.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says מנחם went to the king's service, and eighty pairs of students in silk clothing went with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: מנחם left for the king's service, and eighty pairs of students dressed in silk went out with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says just what רבא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses רבא's exact words, 'the king's service,' so רבא's view has an earlier source behind it. It adds that many students left with מנחם, dressed in fancy royal clothing.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way (a ברייתא supports this)
Pairs
Silk garments

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
מנחם left for the king's service,
and eighty pairs of students went out with him
dressed in silk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's answer in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that מנחם went to the king's service.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא using the same words.

steps.title: Never take a שבות lightly
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that a שבות should never seem minor. סמיכה on יום טוב is only a שבות, yet the greatest sages of each generation argued about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמן בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A שבות should never be light in your eyes. סמיכה is forbidden only because of a שבות, and still the great ones of the generation argued about it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן draws a lesson from our משנה. The leading sages argued about a rule that is only rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סמיכה on יום טוב is not a Torah-level מלאכה. It is forbidden only as a rabbinic שבות. Still, the leaders of every generation in the משנה took it seriously enough to argue about it. So a rabbinic rule is never small.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic prohibition on שבת or יום טוב
Pressing one's hands on a קרבן's head before it is slaughtered
The greatest sages of the generation

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a general attitude: rabbinic rules carry real weight, as the great sages showed by arguing over one.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: רב שמן בר אבא said that רבי יוחנן said:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם אַל תְּהֵא שְׁבוּת קַלָּה בְּעֵינֶיךָ,
phrases.english: A שבות should never be light in your eyes,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי סְמִיכָה אֵינָהּ אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת,
phrases.english: since סמיכה is forbidden only because of a שבות,
and the great ones of the generation argued about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אַל תְּהֵא שְׁבוּת קַלָּה בְּעֵינֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching based on the סמיכה dispute in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שבות must never be treated as minor, as shown by the great sages' dispute over סמיכה.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן needed to say this. Of course a שבות is serious.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's teaching: it seems to say nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שבות is an accepted rabbinic prohibition, so no one should treat it lightly. Why would רבי יוחנן need to prove that from a dispute of the great sages?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious (why say it?)

phrases.english: It is obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רבי יוחנן's statement in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's teaching that a שבות should not be taken lightly.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Everyone already knows a rabbinic prohibition must be kept, so the teaching seems to add nothing.

steps.title: It was needed for a שבות done for a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the teaching was needed because סמיכה is a שבות done for a מצוה. Even that kind of שבות is serious.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needed it for a שבות of a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what is new in רבי יוחנן's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think a שבות done for a מצוה, like סמיכה on a קרבן, is easier to set aside. רבי יוחנן teaches that even this kind of שבות was taken seriously enough for the great sages to argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic prohibition involved in doing a מצוה
He needed it (to teach this)

phrases.english: He needed it for a שבות of a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to show what is new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A שבות done for a מצוה might be considered light.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a שבות done for a מצוה is serious, as the great sages' dispute shows.

steps.title: This too is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again why רבי יוחנן needed to teach that even a שבות done for a מצוה is serious.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from the last step. It says even a שבות done for a מצוה is obviously still forbidden, so why teach it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said the חידוש was that even a שבות for a מצוה matters. The גמרא says that is also plain, since a rabbinic ban stays a ban whatever the reason. So it still wants to know what new point רבי יוחנן was adding.

keyTerms.meaning: This too
It is obvious

phrases.english: This too is obvious!
phrases.notes: He means even a שבות done for a מצוה is clearly still forbidden, so the answer in the last step is not new.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 19 that רבי יוחנן was teaching that a שבות for a מצוה is serious.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שבות done for a מצוה is still obviously forbidden, so saying so adds nothing new.

steps.title: The dispute is about the שבות, not about סמיכה itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's teaching rules out the view that the sages argued about whether סמיכה is required at all. They really argued about the שבות of doing it on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to reject the one who said they argue about סמיכה itself. It teaches us that they argue about the שבות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reason why רבי יוחנן spoke. He wanted to make clear what the sages were really arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could think the generations of sages argued about whether certain offerings need סמיכה at all. רבי יוחנן's words show that the argument was about the rabbinic ban, the שבות, on doing סמיכה on יום טוב. That is the new point.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude or reject a view
Itself
He teaches us
They argue

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody here says סמיכה is not a מצוה. The question is only what the sages' argument was about: the obligation, or the rabbinic ban on doing it on יום טוב.

phrases.english: To exclude the one who said
they argue about the placing of hands itself,
he teaches us
that it is about the rabbinic ban that they argue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what the argument was about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sages argued about whether סמיכה is required at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sages argued only about the שבות of doing סמיכה on יום טוב.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: סמיכה needs all one's strength
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא learns that סמיכה must be done with full force. Otherwise there would be no reason to forbid it on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: Learn from this that סמיכה must be with all one's strength. If you think full strength is not needed, what is he doing wrong? Let him do סמיכה!
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא draws a new הלכה from the fact that סמיכה is a שבות on יום טוב. He says it must be done with full force.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If סמיכה were just a light touch, it would not look like work at all, so the sages would have no reason to ban it on יום טוב. Since it is banned, it must involve pressing with real force, which counts as using the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this
With all his strength
We require
It enters your mind, you might think

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the question for the rest of the section: how much force does סמיכה need?

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said:
Learn from this that placing hands
we require with all his strength,
for if it enters your mind
that we do not require all his strength,
what is he doing? Let him place his hands!
phrases.notes: Literally "what is he doing?" He means: what is wrong with a light touch? Then it should be allowed on יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new הלכה on the fact, from steps 17 and 21, that סמיכה on יום טוב is a שבות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סמיכה must be done with all of one's strength.

steps.title: A ברייתא about women doing סמיכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רמי בר חמא. Women are not obligated in סמיכה, but רבי יוסי and רבי ישמעאל say they may do it if they choose.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: "Speak to the sons of Israel... and he shall place his hand." The sons of Israel place their hands, and the daughters of Israel do not. רבי יוסי and רבי ישמעאל say: The daughters of Israel may place their hands if they choose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge against רמי בר חמא by quoting a ברייתא. This step is setting up the challenge, which is completed in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'sons of Israel,' so only men are obligated in סמיכה. רבי יוסי and רבי ישמעאל add that women may still do it as an option. That opinion is what the challenge will be built on.

keyTerms.meaning: They place their hands
The daughters of Israel, women
Optional, allowed but not required

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
"Speak to the sons of Israel... and he shall place",
the sons of Israel place their hands,
and the daughters of Israel do not place their hands.
Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Yishmael say:
the daughters of Israel place their hands as an option.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge to רמי בר חמא's statement in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's claim that סמיכה needs all one's strength.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets women do סמיכה even when they are not obligated. The next steps show why that would not work if full strength were required.

steps.title: The story of the women and the calf
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי tells, in the name of אבא אלעזר, that women once did סמיכה on a שלמים calf, only to make them happy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: אבא אלעזר told me: Once we had a calf for a שלמים offering. We brought it to the women's courtyard, and women placed their hands on it. This was not because women do סמיכה, but to give the women a good feeling.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a real event that backs up רבי יוסי's view. It shows women actually did סמיכה even though they were not obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story makes clear that this סמיכה was not the required מצוה. It was done only so the women would feel included. That detail is the key the גמרא will use in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He told me
Peace offerings
The women's courtyard in the בית המקדש
A good feeling, satisfaction

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said,
Abba Elazar told me:
Once we had
a calf for peace offerings,
and we brought it to the women's courtyard,
and women placed their hands on it.
Not because women have placing of hands,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת נַחַת רוּחַ לַנָּשִׁים.
phrases.english: but in order to give the women a good feeling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, סָח לִי אַבָּא אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 23 with a story that supports רבי יוסי.
steps.raayaObject: That women may do סמיכה even though they are not obligated.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An event reported by אבא אלעזר to רבי יוסי.

steps.title: So full strength must not be required
steps.stepSummary: If סמיכה needed full strength, letting women do it just to make them happy would mean using a holy animal for work. So full strength must not be needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think סמיכה needs all one's strength, would we do work with a holy animal just to give women a good feeling? Rather, learn from this that full strength is not required!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge to רמי בר חמא. It uses the women's story to show that סמיכה does not need full force.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pressing hard on an animal counts as using it for work, and that is forbidden with קדשים unless a מצוה requires it. Women had no obligation, so if their סמיכה used full force it would have been forbidden. Since the sages allowed it, סמיכה must not need full strength, which goes against רמי בר חמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Using a holy animal for work, which is forbidden
Rather, is it not so that

steps.whatToRemember: רמי בר חמא says סמיכה needs full strength, because otherwise it could not be a שבות on יום טוב. The ברייתא about the women suggests full strength is not needed, because otherwise it would be forbidden work with קדשים.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that we require placing hands with all his strength,
for the sake of a good feeling for women
would we do work with consecrated animals?
phrases.notes: Pressing hard on the animal counts as making it work, and you can't do that to a holy animal without a מצוה requiring it.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not so? Learn from this
that we do not require all his strength!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ סְמִיכָה בְּכׇל כֹּחוֹ בָּעֵינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the story in step 24 and aims it at step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's claim in step 22 that סמיכה needs all one's strength.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Full-strength סמיכה counts as work with קדשים, which is forbidden without a מצוה. Yet women were allowed to do סמיכה only for a good feeling, so it must not require full strength.

steps.title: The women were told to rest their hands lightly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רמי בר חמא. סמיכה really does need full strength, but the women were told to put their hands on lightly, so it was not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, I can tell you that we do need full strength for סמיכה. Here, though, they told the women: rest your hands lightly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 25 and keeps רמי בר חמא's rule standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said that if the women had leaned with full force, they would have used a holy animal for work. The answer is that they did not lean with force at all; they only rested their hands lightly. So no work was done, and real סמיכה can still require full strength.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (used to keep the original position)
With all his strength
Rest your hands lightly

phrases.english: Really, I can say to you
we do require it with all one's strength
for he told them: Rest your hands lightly.
phrases.notes: Literally "let your hands float." They touched the animal without leaning their weight on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 25 by redefining what the women actually did.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case: the women only rested their hands lightly
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The women did full סמיכה, so it must not need strength
steps.terutzMaskana: The women only touched lightly; real סמיכה can still need full strength

steps.title: Then why not say it wasn't סמיכה at all?
steps.stepSummary: If the women only touched lightly, the ברייתא should have said it wasn't real סמיכה at all, not that it was done to make them happy.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why say "not because women do סמיכה"? Let him say instead that it isn't סמיכה at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 26 by looking at the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the women only touched lightly, the obvious reason it was allowed is that this isn't סמיכה at all. Yet the ברייתא gave a different reason: making the women happy. That suggests the women did real סמיכה, which brings back the problem for רמי בר חמא.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let him derive it from (a simpler reason)
At all

phrases.english: If so,
why say "not because there is סמיכה for women"?
Let him derive it from the fact that it is not סמיכה at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 26 using the ברייתא's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the women only rested their hands lightly
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were true, the ברייתא would have given the simpler reason that this isn't סמיכה at all, not the reason of making the women happy.

steps.title: רבי אמי: The ברייתא gives two reasons
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי explains that the ברייתא means two reasons together: it wasn't real סמיכה, and it was also done to make the women happy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: He is saying one reason and another. One: it isn't סמיכה at all. Another: it was done to please the women.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי answers the question of Step 27 and saves the explanation of Step 26.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא doesn't leave out the reason "it isn't סמיכה at all"; that reason is understood. The words "to please the women" are an extra reason telling us why they bothered doing it at all. So רמי בר חמא's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He is saying one reason, and another as well
Pleasure, satisfaction

steps.whatToRemember: סמיכה needs full strength (רמי בר חמא). The women only touched lightly, so it wasn't real סמיכה, and it was done just to make them happy.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
He is saying one reason, and another.
One: that it is not סמיכה at all,

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד — כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת נַחַת רוּחַ לַנָּשִׁים.
phrases.english: and another: in order to please the women.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: חֲדָא וְעוֹד קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 27 by reading the ברייתא as giving two reasons.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the text as containing two reasons
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא gave only one reason, making the women happy
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא assumes it isn't real סמיכה, and adds that it was done to please the women

steps.title: רב פפא: The sides of the animal are also forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא learns from the story that the ban on using an animal covers its sides too. Otherwise the women could have done full סמיכה on the sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Learn from this that the sides are forbidden. If you thought the sides were allowed, they should have let the women lean on the sides. So it must be that the sides are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא draws a new lesson in הלכה from the story of the women's סמיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The women were only allowed to touch lightly, because leaning would be using the animal. If using the sides of an animal were allowed, they could simply have leaned with full force on the sides. Since they didn't, the sides must be forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this
Sides (of the animal)
If it would enter your mind
Rather, isn't it so that...

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a rule that the ban on using something forbidden covers its sides, not only the main surface.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Learn from this
that the sides are forbidden,
phrases.notes: He means using the sides of the animal is forbidden, just like using its back.

phrases.english: for if it would enter your mind
that the sides are permitted,
let them lean on the sides.
Rather, isn't it so? Learn from this
that the sides are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that the women only touched lightly, and draws a new rule from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on using an animal (here, a holy animal) applies to its sides as well, not only its back.
